text: Occupation: Councilmember & Former Mayor, City of Hermosa Beach/California Coastal Commissioner/Colonel U.S. Army (Retired)

A lifelong public servant, I proudly wore our nation's uniform for over thirty years, retiring as an Army Colonel. For the past eleven years, I have been equally proud to serve our "Best Little Beach City" by coaching hundreds of our kids, volunteering with our School District and dozens of local organizations, and, for the past five and a half years, serving as your City Councilmember and Mayor, in elected regional leadership roles, and as your state-appointed California Coastal Commissioner.
Serving Hermosa Beach has been the honor of a lifetime. Together, we have accomplished so much, but our most important work still lies ahead.

Our city is at a pivotal moment, and the need for competent, experienced leadership has never been greater. The decisions we make today will shape Hermosa Beach for generations to come. That is why I remain committed to thoughtful leadership grounded in fiscal responsibility, public safety, smart and measured growth, and protecting the character, quality of life, and values that make our community so special.
I would be honored to earn your vote once again and continue serving with integrity, experience, common sense, and action.
Thank you for your trust, your support, and the privilege of serving our community. Together, let's keep Hermosa Beach moving onward and upward.

text: Occupation: Boardmember, Hermosa Beach City School District/Non-profit Director

Hermosa residents deserve experienced, responsible, and pragmatic leadership at City Hall. Born and raised in Hermosa Beach, I have dedicated my career to public service, public policy, and law. Over the last 13 years on the Hermosa School Board, including three as Board President, I successfully managed $100M budgets, maintained strong reserves through COVID-19, and spearheaded $87M in facility bonds to modernize our schools.
My priorities for Hermosa Beach include:
Streamlining permit and zoning timelines using a data-driven system to provide predictability for residents and business owners.
Using proven fiscal discipline to transition from reactive budgeting to sustainable, long-term infrastructure and financial planning.
Preserving our unique beach-city character while ensuring a safe, modern future that supports youth, renters, homeowners, and seniors.

I have lived every stage of life here—from renting as a young professional to buying a home, raising a family, and supporting aging parents. I know our community's needs firsthand and would be honored to earn your vote.
Learn more at Maggie4Hermosa.org/ email Maggie4hermosa@gmail.com
Thank you, Maggie

text: Occupation: Hermosa Beach City Councilmember

My wife Katie and I have been blessed to call Hermosa Beach home for 52 years. As a general contractor for five decades. I've built and remodeled homes and businesses across Hermosa. I get things done, on time and on budget.
My qualifications:

- Your Councilmember since 2022; Mayor in 2026
- Board Member, South Bay Cities Council of Governments
- 8 years as Planning Commissioner
- 2 years as Public Works Commissioner
- President, Hermosa Beach Kiwanis Club
I worked to begin a turnaround at City Hall. Spending gets real scrutiny, stalled projects are getting finished, and we are rebuilding a culture of cooperation. There is more to do.
When re-elected, I will work for:

- Careful investment in infrastructure that keeps Hermosa safe, beautiful and economically vibrant
- Protecting public safety while building community trust
- Local control over decisions that belong here in Hermosa
- Smart financial choices that make taxpayer dollars go further
Big decisions are ahead: saving our Pier, tough budget negotiations, major infrastructure work. My unique experience with construction, land use, budgets, and governance really matters now.
I pledge to donate my entire council salary to local projects and good causes. I ask for your trust and your vote.
